authorized_secondary_ml_candidates: behavioral-feature clustering after deterministic field treatment

cross_dataset_policy.future_exception: Only a separately justified and verified common representation may revisit this policy.

decision_basis: N-BaIoT passes P1, P2, and P3; Bot-IoT does not pass P1 or P3 at the required level.
N-BaIoT has a stable ordered numeric schema and a verified zero-exact-vector-overlap feasibility path.
Bot-IoT's 477 benign rows are an intrinsic limitation of the audited local 5% source and cannot be repaired for evaluation by resampling.
Both datasets retain meaningful project value when assigned different roles.

decision_rule.enabling_requirements: P4-P8 must provide a defensible path, with unresolved implementation choices explicitly deferred
decision_rule.limitation_policy: Prefer controllable limitations with verified mitigation paths over intrinsic source-distribution limits that prevent reliable primary evaluation.

mandatory_primary_gates.P1: core binary support must be SUPPORTED
mandatory_primary_gates.P2: a leakage-controlled evaluation candidate must be SUPPORTED
mandatory_primary_gates.P3: reasonable core-class evaluation resolution must be SUPPORTED

deferred_to_g2: lock the primary 115-field representation, order, and provenance contract
decide predictor eligibility and feature selection
select duplicate weighting without blind global deduplication
lock the Bot-IoT representation and field treatment, including ports and unresolved sentinels
materialize the reproducible processed Assignment-2 package and versioned feature contract
deferred_to_g3: adopt the final train, validation, and test protocol; N2 is only the leading audited reference
decide whether device holdout is used as a stress test
select and evaluate classifiers and the final model
select the clustering algorithm, sampling, and evaluation protocol
select and execute at least one bounded Bot-IoT secondary ML experiment
finalize the inference payload after the feature contract and defer Pi claims until benchmarking

intrinsic_or_source_bound: only 477 benign observations exist in the audited local 5% source
data exfiltration, keylogging, and theft labels have 6, 73, and 79 observations
mitigable: representation, risky-field eligibility, and lexical port parsing can be locked deterministically
entity-grouped candidates can control a specified entity boundary

intrinsic_or_source_bound: the audited corpus contains a large exact-duplicate/effective-sample burden
device coverage differs for two devices
mitigable: exact-vector boundary leakage can be controlled by group-aware assignment
scaling, feature selection, sampling, and duplicate weighting remain design choices

primary_constraints: The core supervised objective remains benign versus malicious.
Family and fine labels remain preserved as metadata and analysis labels.
Naive row-random evaluation is prohibited without duplicate-boundary control.
Blind global deduplication is not adopted.
Every future split must check exact-vector boundary leakage or prove an equivalent control.
The 115-column order and feature-generation provenance must be versioned.
N2 is a leading audited candidate and feasibility reference, not the final split.
Device holdout remains a possible stress-test family, not automatically the main protocol.

n2_feasibility.status: leading audited candidate / feasibility reference; not final split

rejected_alternative.reason: For this project's primary role, Bot-IoT fails the present P3 evaluation-resolution gate and only partially supports P1. Entity grouping cannot create additional independent benign or rare-class observations. This is role-specific and does not make Bot-IoT unusable or universally inferior.

role_scope: IoTGuard's core benign-vs-malicious classification, Assignment-2 pipeline, and later structured-feature deployment
secondary_constraints: attack, category, and subcategory are target metadata and not ordinary predictors.
pkSeqID and the unnamed physical index are lineage/identifier metadata and excluded from ordinary predictors unless a future ADR explicitly overturns this.
Treatment of stime, ltime, seq, addresses, ports, and other context fields remains deferred.
Hexadecimal ports require deterministic lexical-aware parsing if retained.
The semantics of the -1 port token remain unresolved.
A representation must be explicitly locked before any official experiment.
The supplied split is not considered proven leakage-free.
secondary_ml_requirement: G2/G3 must select and execute at least one technically defensible Bot-IoT ML experiment; the secondary dataset may not be used only for EDA.
